newsitem.title: JAPAN: View on Japan recovery trend backed by tankan -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: View on Japan recovery trend backed by tankan -- BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economy in general is in a trend of gradual recovery, and this view was backed up by the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey this week, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Friday.

He also said in a speech to business executives that there was no need for concern that a fund flight from Japan would accelerate only because of an interest rate differential between Japan and overseas.

He said the current floating exchange rate system should stem any one-sided capital outflow. Japan's foreign investment had increased as a result of the expanding interest rate gap between the United States and Japan, but this had not choked off domestic funds or tended to push up domestic interest rates for a long time, he said.
Matsushita said the BOJ's monetary policy was geared to strengthening Japan's economic recovery and ensuring sustainable, non-inflationary economic growth.
Japan's domestic prices were likely to remain stable for now, helped by the recent strength of the yen as well as stable oil prices, he said.

He said there was only a small possibility that the sales tax rise or the halting of special income tax cuts would destroy the current recovery trend in consumption, given recent improvement in the income environment.

Matsushita said the private sector needed to strengthen its self-sustaining recovery momentum in order to get the economy back on a sustainable recovery track at a time when public spending had been curbed and the sales tax had been raised.
"We are now at the stage of monitoring (private-sector activity) from this perspective," he said.

Matsushita said the current slowing down of Japan's economy was likely to be temporary, adding that the economy was highly likely to sustain its recovery trend. But he also said on this point that the BOJ needed to see actual movements in consumer spending and corporate activity to form a judgment.

Matsushita said monetary policy should not overemphasise the stability of foreign exchange rates or asset prices. "If we set the stability (of foreign exchange rates and asset prices) as the direct objective of monetary policy we risk damaging the stability of the domestic economy."
He added that movements in foreign exchange rates and asset prices should be adjusted through market mechanisms and that it was undesirable to try to control them through monetary policy.
